messages:
mira: quick heads-up — our canary for magnet16b-int4-hybrid shows a reproducible divergence when priming with short interleaved messages (system->user->assistant pattern). fails after ~18k tokens consistently :frowning:
cheng: fwiw does the same trace exist on float32 build? or only quantized?
mira: only appears on int4-hybrid. float32 and int8 runs are clean on the same prompt. attaching minimal log below.

mira: ```
# run: ./tools/long_priming_check.sh --model magnet16b-int4-hybrid --seed 42 --window 65536
[init] kv-window=65536 ropescale=1.0
[step 1] priming tokens 0..512 (system)
[step 2] priming tokens 513..768 (user)
[step 3] priming tokens 769..1024 (assistant)
...
[gen] token 18432 expected="the" got="\uFFFD"   <-- divergence: attention scores shifted
[err] kv-index=18432 slot=18432 ropescale=0.99998
``` 

sam: interesting. that ropescale number is suspicious — tiny drift accumulating. could be quant rounding in rotary embeddings or interpolation when we shrink/compact KV pages.
tej: do we have a repro that toggles only the interleaving? like same content but all user messages batched vs interleaved one-by-one?
mira: yes — batched priming (concatenate system+user+assistant) does not diverge. it's specifically the 3-way interleaved pattern.
cheng: hypothesis: when tokens from different roles get written across page boundaries, int4 packing + stride rounding causes a per-token phase offset. over long sequences that accumulates -> token id shift. also check wraparound handling for rotation indices.
sam: can we test with forced ropescale=1.0 (no scaling) in int4 path to see if it's purely scaling math?

mira: tried that — forcing ropescale=1.0 in kernel gave delayed divergence (still happens but at ~46k). so it's not only ropescale but a cumulative quantization/packing effect + boundary handling.
tej: maybe a collision in key hashing when packing pages. do we log raw kv-keys? we should snapshot KV keys at page boundaries.

devops-bot: deploy/canary magnet16b-int4-hybrid: 1 failure (repro) -> rollback queued :warning:

mira: adding snapshotter to the harness now. small diff — dumps first 4 page keys and last 4 every page flip.

mira: ```diff
--- a/runtime/kv_page_manager.cc
+++ b/runtime/kv_page_manager.cc
@@
 void PageFlip() {
-  // old
+  // debug: snapshot keys
+  DumpPageKeys(page->id, /*first_n=*/4, /*last_n=*/4);
   Compact(page);
 }
```

cheng: nice. also add a unit that feeds alternating short messages (len 12-120 tokens) vs long single block to compare.
sam: for triage, i can run a small grid: int4-hybrid quantize-bias={on,off} ropescale={auto,1.0,0.9999} page_size={4096,8192,16384} on a 24h run (send to ci-gpu-large). will post heatmap.
tej: add an eval hook that computes a "fingerprint diff" metric per token (cosine between float32 hidden vs quant hidden) and threshold alerts. that would help detect early drift in canaries.

mira: created an eval job id=eva-31555-priming-fprint with the fingerprint diff. quick sample shows mean cosine drops from 0.997 (float32 vs int4 shadow) to 0.88 around the failure window.
cheng: 0.88 is significant. can we isolate whether it's in attention or in rotary application? instrument attention matmul norm and rotary application separately.
mira: will instrument next. adding two dumps: "attn_qk_norm" and "rotary_phase_offset" every 2k tokens.

sam: one more thought — are we confident the tokenizer isn't shard-splitting tokens differently between steps? sure it's same tokenizer instance? sometimes role-boundary whitespace causes subtle tokenization differences when messages are split.
mira: confirmed tokenizer consistent. the divergence persists even when we concatenate and re-split deterministically.

tej: ok action list:
- sam: run grid and post heatmap in this thread (ETA 8h)
- mira: push page-key snapshot + rotary/attn dumps to canary (ETA 2h)
- cheng: add unit test for interleaved vs batched priming (ETA EOD)
- tej: add fingerprint-diff alert to canary pipeline (ETA 24h)

mira: assigning follow-ups in taskboard -> ML-3782. I'll keep logs in s3://redwood-ml/canaries/3155559999/
cheng: :thumbsup: ping if you need extra GPU for the long run.
sam: starting grid now. will post preliminary heatmap link once first 3 runs finish.
tej: thanks everyone — good catch. if this is KV packing boundary related we should treat as p0 for int4-hybrid bring-up.
mira: agreed. moving to p0 until root cause identified. :eyes:
